title: Optimize Assumption Validation Playbook (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This working playbook documents the concrete validation steps for the Optimize cost model assumptions. Goal is to produce a repeatable set of checks that engineering + finance can run before we lock model parameters for the next pricing/commit cycle. This is intentionally pragmatic: what data do we need, how to calculate each assumption, acceptable ranges, and who signs off.

Scope:
- Hosted API token economics, Dedicated GPU pool cost allocation, and the caching/batching assumptions that materially affect per-token unit costs.
- NOT in scope: long-term hardware procurement forecasts, sales discounts, or per-customer negotiated pricing (these are downstream).

Background/Why this came up:
Recent sensitivity runs showed unit cost swings of ~20–40% driven primarily by 1) batch size distribution and 2) KV cache hit rate. Finance has requested a documented validation of the input data sources and calibration experiments prior to accepting the updated per-token rates for the 2025 commit packages.

Key data sources (priority order) and how to extract a reproducible sample:
1) Billing export (GCP/AWS): monthly line items for GPU instance hours, storage, and egress. Query: billing_export.project = 'redwood-hosted' AND sku_description CONTAINS 'GPU' GROUP BY month. Expected fields: month, provider_cost_usd, region, instance_type.
2) Serving telemetry (Prometheus + Clickhouse): per-request latency, token counts, batch_size histogram. Query example (Clickhouse): SELECT model, bucket AS batch_size, count() FROM requests WHERE ts BETWEEN X AND Y GROUP BY model, batch_size.
3) KV cache metrics (Redis/Holistic telemetry): cache_hits, cache_misses, avg_ttfb. Pull 30-day rolling windows and compute weighted hit-rate by model.
4) Request mix (API logs): percent streaming vs sync, percent embeddings, percent chat vs completion. Filter by route tag in request metadata.
5) Spot/Preemptible reclaim logs: fraction of hours served on spot instances, eviction rate, and effective hourly cost after reprovisioning overhead.
6) Storage/Checkpoint costs: S3/GCS object counts and size for active model artifacts (quantized vs full) per model family.

Assumptions to validate (each item -> data source + validation method + expected range):
A) Average tokens per request (hosted API): source = API logs sample (30d). Validation = compute median and 95th percentile; expected median range by use-case: 12–120 tokens. If median > 120, flag for review (likely batching/streaming confusion).
B) Batch size distribution: source = serving telemetry histograms. Validation = re-run simulator that replays the exact request timestamps and compute effective throughput and latency with current batching settings. Expected mean batch size: 4–32 depending on traffic shape. If effective cost delta > 10% vs model, escalate.
C) KV cache hit rate (prefix/kv cache): source = cache metrics + trace sampling. Validation = instrument a 7-day live A/B where we disable prefix caching for a small percent of traffic and measure token generation delta and cost. Expected hit rate: 18–65% by model; capture model-specific ranges.
D) Quantization compression factor: source = model artifact sizes (quantized artifact size / fp32 baseline). Validation = on-disk size check + inference throughput test to confirm latency tradeoffs. Expected compression: 2–4x; if perf drop > 15% for same model, mark as special-case.
E) GPU utilization uplift from batching: source = telemetry + simulation. Validation = run cost simulator (see linked repo) with real histograms. Expected typical uplift: 1.2–2.4x effective token throughput per GPU.
F) Spot instance effective cost: source = billing export + spot reclaim logs. Validation = compute weighted average hourly cost including reprovisioning (time-to-recover * critical-path penalty). If effective cost within 10% of on-demand, mark as usable.

Calibration experiments (recommended minimal set to run before sign-off):
1) Replay simulation (2 weeks of requests) with: baseline policy, +50% batch_size_limit, reduced batch_delay_ms, and disabled kv cache. Output: per-token cost delta, p50/p95 latency delta, and GPU-hours consumed. Responsible: Miguel. ETA: 2 wks.
2) Live micro-A/B for KV cache (1% traffic) to measure real hit delta and tail impact on latency. Duration: 7 days. Responsible: Evelyn + SRE.
3) Quantization perf test: pick 3 representative models (small/med/large) and run 1k inference runs across seq lengths 64/512/2048; collect latency and error/regression (if any). Responsible: Applied ML (Noah).
4) Spot cost reconciliation: reconcile last 3 months of billing with spot reclaim logs to produce effective hourly cost. Responsible: Finance (Priya) + Infra.

Finance sign-off checklist (draft):
- [ ] Data lineage: raw query + aggregation notebooks for each input are linked and reproducible.
- [ ] Sensitivity table: for each assumption the model produces cost +/- 10% and +/- 25% columns.
- [ ] Reconciled billing: GPU costs used in the model reconcile to billed GPU line items within 3% (after allocation rules).
- [ ] Risk register: top 5 assumptions that move unit cost > 15% explicitly called out with mitigation.
- [ ] Owner & date: every assumption has an owner and a date for revalidation (90 day cadence).

Unresolved questions / risks (needs discussion at next sync):
- Attribution rule for Dedicated pools: how to apportion idle GPU-hour cost across committed customers vs burst. Current draft uses simple proportional allocation by assigned capacity; Finance requested a marginal-cost allocation appendix.
- Handling of low-volume tail models: the model currently applies a blended GPU-hour rate; this disguises large variance. Proposal: separate SKU for low-volume (<0.1% request share) models.
- Live migration costs for private deployments (on-prem support): we currently default to none — finance insists on explicit migration amortization for first-year contracts.

Decision log (short, add entries as we decide):
- 2025-02-20: Decided to use median tokens per request for pricing baseline instead of mean (owner: Asha). Rationale: reduces skew from long-tail interactive sessions.
- 2025-02-27: Agreed to include spot reallocation overhead of 12 minutes per reclamation in effective hourly cost (owner: Priya).

Example sensitivity snapshot (single-row narrative):
- Base: model-x, median tokens=48, batch mean=12, kv_hit=32%, quant_factor=3. Effective unit cost = $0.0018/token.
- If kv_hit increases by 10 pts -> unit cost drops to $0.00155/token (~14% reduction).
- If mean batch size falls by 50% -> unit cost increases to $0.0023/token (~28% increase).

Practical notes and gotchas (from past calibrations):
- Do not mix sampling windows across major product launches (e.g., Dec holiday surge) with steady-state epochs; use rolling 28-day windows for baselining.
- Telemetry histograms are sensitive to aggregation buckets. Prefer raw-event exports for simulator inputs.
- When simulating batch behavior, replay timestamps at original resolution; aggregated per-minute inputs under-estimate peak batching opportunities.

Next steps and owners:
- Miguel: kick off replay simulation with last 14 days (ETA 2025-03-10).
- Evelyn + SRE: schedule KV cache micro-A/B and set tracing (ETA 2025-03-12).
- Noah: pre-run quantization perf tests and upload artifacts (ETA 2025-03-14).
- Priya (Finance): run billing reconciliation for last 3 months and confirm spot overhead parameter (ETA 2025-03-07).

Meeting request: schedule 30-min sign-off review 2025-03-17 to present calibrated model and sensitivity table to Finance (Priya), Product (Asha), Applied ML (Noah), Infra (Miguel), and SRE (Evelyn).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep one canonical Jupyter notebook that takes raw exports and outputs the full sensitivity table + CSV of per-assumption inputs. Link it in Confluence.
- We will probably need to add a "low-volume model" carve-out to the costing UI; chat with Console team after sign-off.

End of WIP playbook.
